articles.description:
When I lived in Belfast, I had one problem: I wanted to know what was showing at the Strand Cinema without having to remember to check their website. I wanted to look at next Friday in my calendar and see if there was anything worth going to.
So I built a scraper. Pull the listings, transform them into something structured, generate an ICS file. Done.
That was June 2023. That workflow—retrieve, transform, output—is still the foundation of everything Clusterflick does today.
I currently have 14 cinema calendar feeds in my Google Calendar. When I want to see what's on, I toggle a few of them on—maybe the BFI, Castle Cinema, Genesis Cinema, and the Prince Charles Cinema if I'm planning for the weekend. When I book tickets, I just copy that event over to my personal calendar.

articles.author: Luigi | Full Stack Web Developer
articles.description:
Hi everyone! 👋
I’m making a big move. For a long time, my world was made of flour, water, and 3:00 AM alarms. As an apprentice baker, I learned that great results require two things: patience and precision.
Now, I’m bringing that same "craftsman" mindset to the world of Web Development.
Actually, more than I thought!
The Recipe = The Code: If you miss one gram of salt, the bread fails. If you miss one semicolon, the script breaks.
The Fermentation = Debugging: You can't rush it. You have to observe, wait, and understand what's happening under the surface.
The Final Product: There’s no better feeling than seeing something you built from scratch being enjoyed by others.
I’ve focused my energy on mastering the "ingredients" of the web:
HTML5 & CSS3 (Semantic layout & Flexbox/Grid)
Bootstrap 5 (Building responsive interfaces that look as good as a fresh croissant!)
I’m currently "kneading" my first lines of JavaScript logic. It’s a challenge, but I’m enjoying the process of making my pages interactive.
I’m excited to join this community, learn from all of you, and eventually land my first role as a Junior Front-End Developer.
If you have any tips for a baker-turned-coder, or just want to say hi, I’d love to connect in the comments!


  
  
  webdev #beginners #careerchange #frontend #bootstrap
articles.title: From Sourdough to Source Code: My Journey into Web Development 🥐💻

articles.description:
Background


Modern distributed systems frequently replicate data across multiple machines, regions, or user devices. Replication is a fundamental design choice that improves system behavior and user experience.
Why replication matters:
High availability – the system continues working even if some nodes fail
Low latency – users interact with nearby replicas
Offline support – devices can operate while disconnected
Fault tolerance – redundancy prevents data loss
Replication introduces a critical question:
What happens when multiple replicas modify the same data concurrently?
In distributed environments, concurrent updates are not an edge case — they are the norm.
Distributed systems inherently operate under imperfect conditions:
Nodes maintain independent copies of data
Network partitions an…

articles.author: Ofri Peretz
articles.description:
Claude Opus generates vulnerable JWT code every single time — 7 out of 7 runs, always leaking sensitive user data into the token payload. Gemini Flash generates it perfectly every single time — 0 out of 7. Same prompt. Opposite outcomes. 100% consistency on both sides.
That's the kind of finding you miss when you rank AI models by a single number.
We benchmarked 700 AI-generated functions across 5 models from Gemini and Claude — 7 iterations per prompt, 20 security-critical tasks, 332 ESLint rules. The aggregate leaderboard says the cheapest model is the safest and both Gemini models are the worst. Then we looked at the data by domain — and the leaderboard fell apart.
This is Part 3 of the AI Security Benchmark Series. Parts 1-2 established a 65-75% vulnerability baseline using Claude-only…
articles.title: We Ranked 5 AI Models by Security. The Leaderboard Is Wrong.

Hey DEV 👋
I want to share a small story about how I started building AeroTools — a free PDF tools website for students and professionals.
In India, many students and job applicants need to upload PDFs for:
Government forms
College admissions
Job applications
Exams
But most websites either:

❌ Ask for login

❌ Limit usage

❌ Show too many ads  
It was frustrating.
So I decided to build my own solution.
I used:
React for frontend
Node.js + Express for backend
PDF processing libraries
Main focus:

🔒 Secure

🆓 Free

📱 Mobile friendly

✅ Compress PDF

✅ Convert PDF to Word/Excel

✅ Merge & Split PDFs

✅ No watermark

✅ No login  
Website: 👉 https://tryaerotools.com

Free • No watermark • No login
(Please share feedback 🙏)
Building was easy.
Getting users was HARD.
At first:
0 visitors
0 feedback
0 motivation 😅
But I learned:
📌 You must share your work

📌 You must listen to users

📌 You must improve daily  
Some lessons so far:
Simple UI > Fancy UI
Speed matters a lot
Trust is everything
Marketing is as important as coding
I’m still improving AeroTools.
If you have time, please try it and tell me:
👉 What feels confusing?

👉 What feature is missing?

👉 What should I improve first?
Thanks for reading ❤️

Happy coding!
